transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Rafael Ortiz, Leah Park (Redwood) — Priya Nair, Tom Ellis, Sara Lim, Jamal Reed (Arkhaven)

Auto-summary (auto): security intake, PHI considerations, KMS + SSO questions.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, quick round-robin?
00:06 Tom Ellis: tom here, cto at arkhaven. we'll be owning the integration with our data plane.
00:10 Priya Nair: priya — security. focused on compliance, PHI handling.
00:14 Sara Lim: sara, cloud architect — i'll own network and infra details.
00:17 Jamal Reed: jamal, devops, here to ask about k8s, peering stuff.
00:20 Rafael Ortiz: rafael, solutions eng at redwood. i'll cover private/dedicated options and k m s.
00:25 Leah Park: leah — performance runbook and benchmarks.
00:28 Maya Chen: great, thanks. goal today is to understand your compliance gates and hosting constraints so we can recommend hosted, dedicated, or private. please call out PHI early — that matters.

01:02 Priya Nair: yes PHI is core to our risk model. we are covered under HIPAA and have internal HITRUST mapping. we need to know if redwood can sign BAAs, where logs live, and how encryption keys are managed.
01:15 Maya Chen: understood. we have a pathways offering: hosted api is simplest but may not meet your key control needs; dedicated reserved capacity gives isolation and VPC options; private deployment (VPC or on-prem) gives you full control. we can sign b a a for enterprise dedicated/private customers — i'll confirm legal.
01:40 Tom Ellis: okay, so high level — if we go hosted we lose key custody? are keys ever shared for hosted?
01:48 Rafael Ortiz: for hosted by default we manage keys; we use envelope encryption and the storage layer is encrypted at rest. we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-kms) for dedicated and private deployments — meaning the KMS is in your account or on-prem and we never persist plaintext keys. for hosted we can discuss a BYOK integration depending on commitment, but typically that is dedicated/private only.
02:20 Priya Nair: BYOK is a hard ask — we need to control rotation and revocation. also, audit logs for who accessed what model and prompt-level logging, plus retention rules. how granular are your logs?
02:33 Leah Park: logs include request metadata, model version, user token id (if provided), timestamps, and per-route latency. we redact PII by default if you opt in to data controls. retention is configurable on dedicated/private — hosted has standard retention windows but we can evaluate contract terms.
03:05 Sara Lim: can you map that to our retention policy? we need 7 years for some audit trails, others shorter — is long-term export possible?
03:15 Rafael Ortiz: yes — on dedicated/private you can export logs to your s3 or logging cluster. for hosted we provide log export hooks (kafka/s3) but long-term retention beyond our SLA typically done by customer export. we'll send documentation.

04:02 Tom Ellis: what about SSO? we use Okta and SAML for console access and provisioning. do you support SAML for admin and RBAC?
04:13 Maya Chen: yes, we support SAML SSO for the Redwood console. for API credentialing we integrate with enterprise SSO + SCIM for provisioning user accounts and roles. RBAC is configurable — you can map IdP groups to roles (admin, operator, viewer).
04:36 Priya Nair: good. does RBAC extend to model-level permissions and route-level scoping? we want dev teams to hit dev models only and production teams to have stricter controls.
04:48 Rafael Ortiz: role scoping can be per-project and per-model. we can enforce route restrictions and token scoping. in private deployments you can further enforce network-level isolation.

06:00 Jamal Reed: question on network — if we pick dedicated with VPC peering, what traffic flows across peering? is there a tunnel or do we call public endpoints?
06:11 Rafael Ortiz: with dedicated VPC peering your app calls internal endpoints in your vpc via peered route; TLS still applies. for private on-prem our control plane can be customer-managed; runtime sits in your network (air-gapped or private subnet).
06:28 Sara Lim: what about egress? we need assurance tokens and request payloads wont traverse third-party networks.
06:34 Leah Park: for dedicated peering traffic stays in-region and within peered networks; for private deployment all traffic is in your environment. we'll attach architecture diagrams.

08:00 Priya Nair: encryption at rest — you said envelope encryption. do you support HSM-backed keys? key rotation? CMKs?
08:10 Rafael Ortiz: yes, we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, and Azure Key Vault; HSM-backed CMKs are supported in dedicated/private where the CMK is in your account. rotation policies are configurable and we log key usage; we never store plaintext model weights with customer keys—we use ephemeral data keys for operations.
08:42 Priya Nair: do you have attestation for key isolation? and do you document key usage for audits?
08:49 Maya Chen: we provide key usage logs and can include them in audit packages for dedicated/private customers; we'll include sample reports in the follow-up.

10:15 Tom Ellis: latency vs cost — if we do dedicated with quantized models, what's the expected qps and p99 latency for a 2k token prompt?
10:26 Leah Park: rough ballpark depends on model family; for our current LLMX-7B quantized profiles we see 60–120 ms per token on A100-class GPUs in dedicated when batching is optimized. p99 for single-request small batches can be 300–500ms overall; we'll run a targeted test with your prompt set and give concrete numbers.
10:55 Tom Ellis: okay, perf test is critical.

12:00 Priya Nair: on compliance, do you hold SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? can you share reports?
12:08 Maya Chen: yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications for our control plane — certified artifacts are available under NDA/secure portal. for dedicated/private some controls sit with the customer (shared responsibility). we'll send the cert bundles.
12:25 Priya Nair: we need to see control mappings to HITRUST/HIPAA — i don't expect a perfect 1:1 but a mapping helps.
12:33 Maya Chen: agreed, we'll attach a compliance mapping doc to HIPAA/HITRUST for review.

14:00 Jamal Reed: what about data residency? some datasets remain in eu-west only. can we pin model execution regionally?
14:08 Rafael Ortiz: yes — requests can be routed to region-specific endpoints. in dedicated/private you can control region placement. hosted customers can request region constraints as part of enterprise agreements.

15:10 Sara Lim: are there any known gaps for healthcare customers you recommend?
15:16 Leah Park: typical gaps are around prompt-level logging and PII retention policies — we usually advise enabling prompt redaction and customer-side tokenization, and exporting logs to your archive for long-term retention.

16:50 Priya Nair: ok on redaction. but we need deterministic deletion capability — if patient requests deletion, how do we comply?
16:59 Rafael Ortiz: we support deletion requests for customer data in dedicated/private—since you control the data export you can target deletion. hosted has process for data deletion but it involves our data retention pipeline and legal process; we'll document the SLA and steps.

18:30 Tom Ellis: how about model versioning and approvals — can we restrict model rollout to specific teams and approve before switching prod?
18:39 Maya Chen: yes — Redwood Console supports model pinning and canary rollouts; policies can auto-fallback to previous model on regressions. we can gate deployments to roles and require approvals.

20:00 Priya Nair: audit logs need to be tamper-evident. what about log signing or write-once storage?
20:10 Rafael Ortiz: we support exporting logs to your WORM-compliant bucket or SIEM. we can provide signed log digests as part of enterprise packages.

22:00 Sara Lim: for SAML flows — do you support multiple IdPs? we have subsidiaries with different Okta instances.
22:07 Maya Chen: yes, multi-IdP is supported and mapping to different orgs/projects is possible.

24:10 Jamal Reed: any constraints on token sizes or request body sizes? we have large structured payloads.
24:16 Leah Park: token limits are model-specific; we can suggest batching or chunking strategies. for heavy structured payloads we recommend embeddings or a hybrid retriever flow to avoid extremely long prompts.

26:00 Tom Ellis: procurement — what does pricing look like for dedicated versus private? we want a ballpark for planning.
26:07 Maya Chen: high-level: hosted is usage-based per-token with baseline SLOs; dedicated has monthly reserved capacity with commit tiers and predictable throughput — private has licensing + support. i'll loop in pricing after we confirm target QPS and model footprint.

28:30 Priya Nair: is there any live customer we can reference in healthcare? reference checks are important.
28:38 Maya Chen: we can share references under NDA; we'll include a reference list for similar regulated customers.

30:00 Rafael Ortiz: short demo — diagram: control plane <-> runtime in customer vpc, kms in customer account, log export to s3, sso to idp. (brief explanation)
30:28 Sara Lim: sketch looks fine, curious about upgrade path — how are runtime patches applied for private?
30:36 Rafael Ortiz: for private we provide an appliance image and upgrade process; we can schedule maintenance windows, and upgrades are orchestrated by our tooling or customer ops depending on deployment model.

33:10 Leah Park: performance testing note — we'll need a sample prompt set and representative tokens. can you share a sanitized dataset?
33:18 Tom Ellis: yes we can produce a redacted sample and a set of success criteria.

35:00 Priya Nair: one more — encryption in transit: TLS only? mTLS options?
35:05 Rafael Ortiz: mTLS available for dedicated/private; hosted supports TLS with mutual auth options for enterprise.

36:30 Maya Chen: summarizing: primary concerns — BYOK/HSM, long-term log retention/export, SAML + SCIM provisioning, RBAC scoping, deletion workflows, HIPAA/HITRUST mapping, region pinning, and perf benchmarks. next steps: we send docs, run a perf test, and meet again.

38:00 Tom Ellis: timeline — we hope to decide by end of Q3. pilot in July if possible.
38:06 Maya Chen: sounds good, we'll target docs and perf tests this week and reconvene w/ results.

40:15 Priya Nair: two smaller items — do you support separate model sandboxes for test teams? and encryption key rotation windows?
40:22 Rafael Ortiz: yes to both — sandboxes map to projects in console; rotation windows are configurable, we recommend 90 days but can align to your policy.

42:00 Sara Lim: what about secrets management for runtime config — do we write secrets into our vault or redwood secrets store?
42:07 Leah Park: you can use your vault and pass secrets via environment variables in private/dedicated; hosted has a managed secret store with encryption. we recommend customer vault for highest control.

44:30 Jamal Reed: any regulatory edge cases we should know about when using embeddings / semantic search over PHI?
44:37 Maya Chen: avoid storing raw PHI in embeddings; recommend tokenization/pseudonymization and store mapping in customer-managed store. embeddings can still leak context, so treat them as sensitive and encrypt/limit access.

46:00 Priya Nair: ok — we'll prepare a list of sample dataset types and decide which are allowed.

48:00 Maya Chen: last logistics — i will email the SOC2/ISO reports, rafael will send private deployment checklist, leah will start benchmark and request sample prompts; tom will provide sample prompts and success criteria.
48:20 Tom Ellis: sounds good.
48:24 Priya Nair: thanks everyone.
48:30 Meeting close.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings, speaker overlap and filler words. Links referenced: security whitepaper (link shared in follow-up), perf spreadsheet (to be shared), private deployment checklist PDF.

Keywords: SOC2, ISO27001, BAA, HIPAA, HITRUST mapping, SAML/SSO, SCIM, RBAC, KMS, BYOK, HSM, VPC peering, dedicated, private, hosted, log export, retention
